# Company 081 — Open-Source License Compliance API

**Company ID:** `company:future:081`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:081`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-081-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no legal determination, repository change or software release.

## Business identity
Purpose: inventory open-source components and map license obligations, incompatibilities, attribution/notice needs and policy risks into developer workflows.

## Product tree
License/SBOM Scanner; Repository/Lockfile Scanner; Container Scanner; Transitive License Graph; License Identification; Compatibility/Policy Rules; Copyleft/Source-Distribution Flagging; Attribution/Notice Generator; Obligation Tracker; License Change Monitor; CI/CD Gate; Developer Guidance; Exception/Legal Review Queue; Acquisition/Portfolio Scan; API/SDK/CLI; Enterprise/Private Deployment; Policy Packs.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree
Features: component/version/source/hash, direct/transitive path, declared/detected license, confidence, license text hash, obligations, distribution mode, linking/use context, policy classification, incompatibilities, exception approval, notices, source-offer requirement flags and evidence.
Customers: software vendors, enterprises, SaaS, embedded/device companies, agencies, open-source-heavy teams, legal/compliance and DevSecOps.
Verticals: cloud/SaaS, mobile, desktop, firmware/embedded, libraries/SDKs, containers, AI software, developer tools.

## Brain capability / architecture
Brain may summarize licenses and flag questions; deterministic policy mapping can identify known obligations, but legal conclusions require qualified review. Architecture: component/SBOM graph, license corpus/versioning, text/fingerprint matcher, policy/compatibility engine, usage/distribution metadata, notice generator, CI gate and evidence ledger.

## Agent tree
Inventory Agent; License Identification Agent; Policy Mapping Agent; Compatibility Agent; Notice/Attribution Agent; Change Monitor; Developer Guidance Agent; Legal-Review Router; Audit Agent.

## Deterministic services
SBOM/lock parsing; package/source hashes; license text fingerprints; SPDX-like identifiers; dependency graph; policy rules; obligation templates; notice aggregation; version/change tracking; CI pass/fail by company policy.

## Workflow
Scan exact build/source → resolve components/transitives → identify license/evidence → map usage/distribution context → evaluate organization policy/compatibility → generate obligations/notices → route ambiguity/high-risk to legal review → gate release under approved policy → preserve build-specific compliance evidence → monitor dependency/license changes.

## Integrations / API / data
Git/CI, package registries, SBOM, containers, build systems, dependency risk platform, artifact registry and legal/compliance systems. Data: components, licenses, texts/hashes, dependency paths, policies, decisions, notices and evidence.

## Monetization / distribution
Repos/builds/components, seats, enterprise/private, API, policy/legal-workflow packs and managed inventory. Distribution via Git/CI/DevSecOps/legal-tech ecosystems.

## Security/privacy/compliance
Source/dependency metadata may be confidential. Keep code private, scan minimal metadata/content, tenant isolate, version evidence. Product supports compliance workflow and does not replace legal advice.

## Failure / edge cases
Missing/incorrect package metadata, dual licensing, custom licenses, vendored code, copied snippets, generated code, license changed between versions, dependency path differs by platform, static/dynamic linking ambiguity, SaaS-only vs distributed software distinctions.

## Scale / overlap
Repo scanner → enterprise compliance → component/license intelligence infrastructure. Overlap #080 dependency risk and #053 release. #081 owns license obligations/policy.

## Classification
**DESIGN NOW:** dependency/artifact provenance, license metadata slot, policy/evidence, build identity and legal-review state.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center dependency/artifact registry should retain license/source metadata for future portfolio builds.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** license corpus, scanner and policy engine.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** commercial legal packs/customer repos/UI/pricing.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** large cross-ecosystem license intelligence graph.

# Mandatory 24-part completion block
1. Product Tree: SBOM/repo/container/transitive/identify/policy/copyleft/notices/obligations/change/CI/guidance/review/API.
2. Feature Tree: component/version/source/hash/path/license/confidence/text/obligations/distribution/policy/exceptions/notices/evidence.
3. Customer Tree: software/enterprise/SaaS/device/agency/OSS-heavy/legal/DevSecOps.
4. Vertical Tree: cloud/mobile/desktop/embedded/SDK/container/AI/devtools.
5. Brain Tree: summarization/question flagging; legal conclusions human-qualified.
6. Agent Tree: inventory/identify/policy/compatibility/notices/change/guidance/review/audit.
7. Service Tree: SBOM/lock parsers/hashes/fingerprints/IDs/graphs/rules/templates/aggregation/versioning/CI.
8. Workflow Tree: scan→identify→context→policy→obligations→review→release gate→evidence→monitor.
9. Integration Tree: Git/CI/registries/SBOM/containers/build/dependency/artifact/legal.
10. Data Tree: components/licenses/texts/paths/policies/decisions/notices/evidence.
11. API Tree: scan/components/licenses/policy/notices/evidence.
12. Monetization Tree: repos/builds/components/seats/enterprise/API/managed.
13. Distribution Tree: Git/CI/DevSecOps/legal-tech/OEM.
14. Automation Tree: inventory/mapping/notices automatic; ambiguous legal determinations routed.
15. Moat Tree: license corpus/fingerprints, policy mappings, ecosystem coverage.
16. Platform Tree: scanner→license compliance OS→software rights infrastructure.
17. Risk Tree: false legal conclusion/missed component/private code exposure/stale license.
18. Scale Tree: repo→enterprise→cross-ecosystem graph.
19. Spinoff Tree: notice generator/license-change feed; dependency risk remains separate.
20. Command Center Dependencies: dependency registry, artifacts, build identity, policy, evidence.
21. Design-Now Requirements: license/source/provenance fields in reusable component manifests.
22. Build-Now Requirements: add license metadata hooks to Command Center build/dependency provenance.
23. Safe-to-Defer Requirements: legal corpus/customer scanners/commercial workflow.
24. Autonomous Mature State: inventories/notices/policy checks run continuously; humans review ambiguous licenses and approve legal exceptions.

## Saturation result
Further branches converge into dependency risk, release and legal-review workflow rather than new portfolio companies.

# Company 082 — Backup Integrity Verification Service

**Company ID:** `company:future:082`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:082`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-082-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no customer restore, backup deletion, failover or production mutation.

## Business identity
Purpose: prove backups are complete, decryptable, internally consistent and actually restorable—not merely present.

## Product tree
Backup Inventory; Coverage/Gap Monitor; Freshness/RPO Monitor; Encryption/Key Readiness; Integrity/Checksum Verification; Database Restore Drill; File/Object Restore Drill; Application Restore Drill; Config/Secret Dependency Check; Isolated Recovery Sandbox; RTO Measurement; Immutable/Ransomware Resilience Check; Dependency Recovery Graph; Scheduled DR Drills; Recovery Runbooks; Evidence/Certification Reports; Alerting; API/SDK; Enterprise/Private Deployment; Provider/Workload Packs.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree
Features: protected system, backup set/version, source, destination, schedule, RPO/RTO targets, encryption/key refs, immutable state, size/count/hash, dependency manifests, restore environment, restore result, application validation tests, duration, gaps, failures and evidence.
Customers: SaaS, enterprises, MSPs, IT/SRE, regulated organizations, database-heavy platforms and cloud teams.
Verticals: databases, file systems, object storage, SaaS exports, application stacks, Kubernetes/cloud, data warehouses and critical business systems.

## Brain capability / architecture
Brain may analyze failure causes and recommend recovery improvements. Backup integrity/restore validation must use deterministic checks and actual isolated restores. Architecture: provider adapter registry, backup catalog, manifest/hash verification, KMS/reference checks, ephemeral recovery sandbox, dependency graph, restore orchestrator, validation suite, cleanup, evidence ledger and protected production restore gate.

## Agent tree
Backup Inventory Agent; Coverage Agent; Integrity Agent; Restore Drill Agent; Database Verifier; Application Verifier; Dependency Agent; RPO/RTO Analyst; Ransomware Resilience Agent; Recovery Planner; Evidence Agent; Incident Agent.

## Deterministic services
Checksum/hash verification; manifest counts; decrypt probe; sandbox provisioning; restore scripts; schema/file comparison; application smoke tests; timers; cleanup; idempotency; drill scheduler; evidence signing.

## Workflow
Inventory protected systems → map required backup/dependencies → check freshness/immutability/encryption → select safe drill → provision isolated recovery env → restore → run deterministic integrity/application tests → measure RPO/RTO → tear down securely → record gaps/evidence → remediate plan → repeat until verified; production restore remains separate protected action.

## Integrations / API / data
Cloud backup services, databases, object/file storage, SaaS exports, Kubernetes, KMS/vaults, infrastructure-as-code, monitoring and incident systems. Data: backup metadata/manifests/hashes/drill results/timings/gaps/evidence; customer backup contents retained only in isolated drill environment as needed.

## Monetization / distribution
Protected systems, backup sets, storage size, drills, providers, seats, enterprise/private, compliance reports and managed DR verification. Distribution via cloud/MSP/security/SRE ecosystems.

## Security/privacy/compliance
Recovery sandboxes contain sensitive data: isolate network/account, restrict access, ephemeral credentials, cleanup proof, no production endpoints, encrypted storage and retention limits. A successful checksum alone is never labeled a successful restore.

## Failure / edge cases
Backup exists but key lost, full backup valid/incremental corrupt, restore tooling version mismatch, hidden external dependency, application boots but data inconsistent, replica snapshot stale, malware in backup, restore quota/capacity unavailable, backup policy changed without catalog update.

## Scale / overlap
Single DB drill → enterprise DR verification → recovery assurance infrastructure. Overlap #49 reliability, #53 release/migrations, #78 retention, Command Center Recovery Category 14. #082 owns proof of restorability.

## Classification
**DESIGN NOW:** backup/restore evidence, recovery-point identity, dependency manifests, isolation, RPO/RTO fields and drill vs production-restore separation.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center recovery architecture must prove restore, not just backup existence; reverse-map makes recovery drills mandatory foundation.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** customer provider adapters and sandbox orchestration.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** commercial backup packs/UI/pricing.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** large distributed drill fleet and cross-region recovery assurance.

12. Monetization Tree: systems/backups/size/drills/providers/seats/enterprise/managed.
13. Distribution Tree: cloud/MSP/security/SRE/OEM.
14. Automation Tree: drills/validation automatic; production restore gated.
15. Moat Tree: provider restore knowledge, dependency manifests, drill outcome corpus.
16. Platform Tree: backup checker→DR verifier→recovery assurance infrastructure.
17. Risk Tree: false restore confidence/data leak/key loss/sandbox escape/cleanup failure.
18. Scale Tree: workload→enterprise→cross-region/global.
19. Spinoff Tree: recovery runbook/dependency graph modules; reliability/retention remain adjacent.

# Company 083 — Domain / DNS / SSL Autopilot

**Company ID:** `company:future:083`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:083`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-083-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no registrar, DNS, certificate, mail-authentication or domain ownership changes.

## Business identity
Purpose: prevent internet-infrastructure failures and hijacks by continuously monitoring domains, DNS, TLS certificates, nameservers, DNSSEC and mail-related DNS configuration.

## Product tree
Domain Inventory; Registrar/Renewal Monitor; Ownership/Lock Monitor; DNS Zone Monitor; Record Drift; DNSSEC Monitor; Nameserver Health; TLS/Certificate Monitor; CAA; Redirect/HTTP Endpoint Check; Subdomain Inventory; MX/SPF/DKIM/DMARC Health; Propagation/Change Verification; Hijack/Tamper Detection; Expiration Alerts; Change Planner; Approved Auto-Remediation; Evidence/History; API/SDK; MSP/Multi-Tenant; Enterprise/Private Deployment.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree
Features: domain/zone/provider/account refs, registrar, expiry/auto-renew state, lock status, nameservers, DNS records/TTL, DNSSEC, cert issuer/SAN/expiry/chain, CAA, mail records, HTTP/TLS health, change history, expected configuration, drift, risk and verification.
Customers: SMBs, SaaS, enterprises, agencies, MSPs, ecommerce, IT/security teams, multi-brand companies and domain portfolio owners.
Verticals: websites/apps, ecommerce, email-heavy businesses, APIs, multi-tenant SaaS, brands/franchises and regulated/public systems.

## Brain capability / architecture
Brain may explain anomalies and recommend corrections; deterministic DNS/TLS parsers/resolvers and expected-state policies own detection. Changes require protected authority because a single wrong record can cause outage/hijack.

Architecture: domain/provider registry, authoritative/public resolver probes, DNS canonical model, certificate scanner, registrar adapters, expected-state/version store, mail-auth parser, propagation verifier, incident state machine and protected change/rollback.

## Agent tree
Domain Inventory Agent; DNS Health Agent; Certificate Agent; DNSSEC Agent; Mail DNS Agent; Drift Agent; Hijack Risk Agent; Propagation Verifier; Change Planner; Incident Agent; QA/Security Agent.

## Deterministic services
DNS resolution; record normalization; TTL/version diff; cert chain validation; expiry timers; DNSSEC checks; SPF/DKIM/DMARC syntax; CAA checks; endpoint probes; provider locks; change idempotency; rollback snapshots.

## Workflow
Inventory → capture expected known-good state → continuously resolve/probe → detect expiry/drift/tamper → classify impact → alert/plan → protected provider change if authorized → verify propagation from independent resolvers → check TLS/app/mail health → rollback/escalate on failure → preserve evidence.

## Integrations / API / data
Registrars, DNS providers, certificate authorities/ACME, CDN/hosting, email providers, monitoring/SIEM. Data: domains, records, cert metadata, provider refs, expected versions, observations, incidents and changes; credentials remain secret refs.

## Monetization / distribution
Domains/zones/certificates, probes, seats, MSP tenants, enterprise/private, API and managed infrastructure monitoring. Distribution through hosting/domain/MSP/security ecosystems.

## Security/privacy/compliance
Registrar/DNS credentials are critical; use least privilege, domain locks, step-up, out-of-band verification, immutable change evidence, no automatic ownership transfer. Avoid exposing internal/private zone data to unauthorized probes.

## Failure / edge cases
Registrar API outage, stale resolver cache, split-horizon DNS, DNSSEC rollover, wildcard cert, ACME failure, certificate chain issue, nameserver migration, propagation variance, deliberate temporary record, expired payment method, subdomain takeover, dangling CNAME, mail-provider migration.

## Scale / overlap
Single domain → multi-brand portfolio → internet-infrastructure control plane. Overlap #84 deliverability, #49 reliability, #73 credential rotation. #083 owns domains/DNS/TLS state.

## Classification
**DESIGN NOW:** provider/account registry, expiring-resource scheduler, expected-state drift, protected infrastructure changes, independent verification and rollback.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center future company factory will own many domains; portfolio registry must support domain/environment/provider refs without mixing companies.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** domain registry/monitoring/credential isolation before any portfolio company launches publicly.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** commercial customer monitoring/remediation product.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** massive global probe network.

# Company 084 — Email Deliverability Autopilot

**Company ID:** `company:future:084`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:084`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-084-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no bulk sending, warm-up scheme, DNS change or marketing execution.

## Business identity
Purpose: continuously measure and improve the technical health of legitimate permission-based email delivery without enabling spam or abusive bulk messaging.

## Product tree
Domain Authentication Monitor; SPF/DKIM/DMARC Analyzer; Domain/IP Reputation Monitor; Bounce/Complaint Monitor; Suppression Health; Blocklist Monitor; Sending-Pattern Analyzer; Provider/Inbox Placement Tests; Alignment/Route Analyzer; Delivery Score; Incident Alerts; Remediation Planner; Postmaster/Feedback Integration; Transactional-vs-Marketing Separation; Dedicated/Shared IP Analysis; Change Verification; API/SDK; Enterprise/Private Deployment; ESP Packs.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree
Features: sending domain/subdomain, provider/account, SPF/DKIM/DMARC state, selector/version, IP/pool, bounce types, complaint rates, suppression state, volume/rate, engagement trends, blocklists, inbox/spam placement samples, reputation signals, route, incident and remediation evidence.
Customers: legitimate SaaS, ecommerce, marketplaces, support systems, transactional-email apps, enterprises, newsletters with consent, agencies managing authorized senders and ESP customers.
Verticals: transactional auth/receipts, support, lifecycle/product messaging, opted-in marketing, marketplaces and notifications. Abuse/spam is prohibited.

## Brain capability / architecture
Brain may diagnose likely causes and recommend safe changes. Deterministic DNS/authentication parsing, provider metrics and policy thresholds own health state. Architecture: domain/sender registry, DNS monitor, ESP/postmaster adapters, event analytics, reputation/blocklist collectors, placement test harness, incident state machine and remediation evidence.

## Agent tree
Authentication Agent; Reputation Agent; Bounce/Complaint Agent; Suppression Agent; Placement Agent; Routing Agent; Incident Agent; Remediation Planner; Compliance/Consent Liaison; QA Agent.

## Deterministic services
SPF/DKIM/DMARC parsers; DNS verification; bounce taxonomy; complaint/suppression rules; rate/volume metrics; blocklist checks; domain alignment; alert thresholds; change tracking; provider health.

## Workflow
Register authorized sender → verify DNS/authentication → ingest delivery/bounce/complaint/suppression telemetry → detect degradation → classify likely source → recommend technical/consent/list remediation → protected DNS/provider change if needed → verify metrics and placement over time → close incident with evidence.

## Integrations / API / data
DNS/domain systems, legitimate ESPs, postmaster/feedback services, suppression systems, CRM/marketing platforms where authorized, analytics and SIEM. Data: sender metadata, DNS/auth state, aggregate delivery events, reputation/placement metrics and incidents; minimize recipient PII.

## Monetization / distribution
Domains/senders, message volume monitored, provider accounts, seats, enterprise/private, API and managed deliverability consulting software. Distribution via ESP/SaaS/ecommerce/agency ecosystems.

## Security/privacy/compliance
Require authorized sender ownership, consent/suppression respect, no evasion of provider anti-abuse controls, no purchased-list or spam optimization. Protect recipient and provider data; DNS/provider changes remain protected.

## Failure / edge cases
DNS propagation, forwarded mail affecting DMARC, provider metric lag, shared IP neighbor reputation, sudden legitimate volume spike, new domain, corporate filtering, temporary blocklist, soft vs hard bounce, complaint feedback gaps, mailbox-provider policy change.

## Scale / overlap
One domain → multi-brand enterprise → deliverability health platform. Overlap #83 domain/DNS, #64 inbox, communications systems. #084 owns sender deliverability health.

## Classification
**DESIGN NOW:** domain/sender/account isolation, consent/suppression metadata, provider health, expiring DNS/key resources and communication evidence.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center future communication factory should track sender identity/domain/provider separately by company.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** sender-domain/authentication monitoring before any portfolio company relies on email at scale.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** customer ESPs/placement network/commercial service.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** large global placement/reputation observatory.

# Mandatory 24-part completion block
1. Product Tree: auth/reputation/bounce/complaint/suppression/blocklist/patterns/placement/alignment/score/alerts/remediation/feedback/API.
2. Feature Tree: domain/provider/SPF/DKIM/DMARC/IP/bounces/complaints/suppression/volume/placement/reputation/incidents/evidence.
3. Customer Tree: SaaS/ecommerce/marketplaces/support/transactional/enterprise/consent newsletters/agencies/ESPs.
4. Vertical Tree: transactional/support/lifecycle/authorized marketing/marketplace/notifications.
5. Brain Tree: diagnosis/recommendation; health facts deterministic/provider-derived.
6. Agent Tree: auth/reputation/bounce/suppression/placement/routing/incident/remediation/compliance/QA.
7. Service Tree: DNS parsers/bounce taxonomy/complaint rules/metrics/blocklists/alignment/thresholds/change tracking.
8. Workflow Tree: register→verify→ingest→detect→diagnose→remediate→protected change→verify→close.
9. Integration Tree: DNS/ESP/postmaster/feedback/suppression/CRM/analytics/SIEM.
10. Data Tree: sender/DNS/auth/events/reputation/placement/incidents.
11. API Tree: sender health/auth/metrics/incidents/recommendations/evidence.
12. Monetization Tree: domains/senders/volume/accounts/seats/enterprise/API/managed.
13. Distribution Tree: ESP/SaaS/ecommerce/agencies/OEM.
14. Automation Tree: monitoring/diagnosis automatic; DNS/provider/communication changes protected.
15. Moat Tree: cross-provider health history, diagnostics, placement coverage, remediation outcomes.
16. Platform Tree: deliverability monitor→autopilot→sender infrastructure health layer.
17. Risk Tree: facilitating spam/wrong diagnosis/DNS outage/privacy leak/reputation damage.
18. Scale Tree: domain→portfolio→global observatory.
19. Spinoff Tree: DMARC/auth monitor/placement network; domain infrastructure remains adjacent.
20. Command Center Dependencies: domains, communication identity, consent, provider registry, observability, incidents.
21. Design-Now Requirements: each company email identity must map to isolated domain/provider/consent/suppression state.
22. Build-Now Requirements: communication factory must include sender-health/consent hooks, not just send capability.
23. Safe-to-Defer Requirements: customer placement network/ESP connectors/commercial product.
24. Autonomous Mature State: sender health is continuously monitored and technical regressions surfaced/fixed under policy; humans manage strategy, consent and high-impact changes.

## Saturation result
Further branches converge into domain/DNS, consent and communications infrastructure already represented.
